annotations.label: Coracoid process
annotations.description: A hook-shaped projection from the superior scapula, lying anterior to the glenoid and serving as an attachment for muscles and ligaments.

annotations.label: Superior angle
annotations.description: The superior angle is where the superior and medial borders of the scapula meet.

annotations.label: Acromion
annotations.description: The acromion continues laterally from the scapular spine and forms the bony roof above the shoulder joint.

annotations.label: Clavicle
annotations.description: An S-shaped subcutaneous strut between the manubrium and acromion that holds the upper limb away from the trunk and transmits load to the axial skeleton.

annotations.label: Intertubercular groove
annotations.description: The groove between the greater and lesser humeral tubercles contains the tendon of the long head of biceps.

annotations.label: Surgical neck
annotations.description: The surgical neck is the narrowed region below the humeral tubercles, close to the axillary nerve and posterior circumflex humeral artery.

annotations.label: Lesser tubercle
annotations.description: The lesser tubercle projects anteriorly from the proximal humerus and receives the subscapularis tendon.

annotations.label: Greater tubercle
annotations.description: The greater tubercle is the lateral prominence of the proximal humerus and receives supraspinatus, infraspinatus and teres minor.

annotations.label: Medial epicondyle
annotations.description: The medial epicondyle projects from the distal humerus and gives origin to the common superficial flexor group.

annotations.label: Lateral epicondyle
annotations.description: The lateral epicondyle projects from the distal humerus and gives origin to the common extensor tendon.

annotations.label: Trochlea
annotations.description: The spool-shaped humeral trochlea articulates with the trochlear notch of the ulna at the elbow.

annotations.label: Coronoid process
annotations.description: The coronoid process forms the anterior projection of the proximal ulna below the trochlear notch.

annotations.label: Deltoid tuberosity
annotations.description: The deltoid tuberosity is a rough lateral shaft prominence that receives the deltoid insertion.

annotations.label: Humerus
annotations.description: The long bone of the arm, articulating with the glenoid proximally and the radius and ulna distally; key landmarks include the surgical neck, radial groove and medial epicondyle.

annotations.label: Ulna
annotations.description: The medial forearm bone, whose olecranon and coronoid process form the trochlear notch around the humeral trochlea; its distal head is separated from the carpus by an articular disc.

annotations.label: Ulna, styloid process
annotations.description: The ulnar styloid process projects distally from the posteromedial aspect of the ulnar head.

annotations.label: Radius, styloid process
annotations.description: The radial styloid process projects distally from the lateral radius on the thumb side of the wrist.

annotations.label: Carpal bones
annotations.description: Eight short bones arranged in proximal and distal rows form the carpus between the forearm and metacarpals.

annotations.label: Radius
annotations.description: The lateral forearm bone in anatomical position, with a disc-shaped head proximally and a broad distal end that articulates with the scaphoid and lunate.

annotations.label: Scapula
annotations.description: A triangular flat bone on the posterolateral thoracic wall, spanning roughly ribs 2–7; its lateral angle bears the glenoid cavity and its spine expands into the acromion.

annotations.label: Inferior angle
annotations.description: The inferior angle is the meeting point of the medial and lateral scapular borders.

annotations.label: Tuberosity of radius
annotations.description: The radial tuberosity lies just distal to the radial neck and receives the biceps brachii tendon.

annotations.label: Capitulum
annotations.description: The rounded lateral articular surface of the distal humerus articulates with the head of the radius.

annotations.label: Head of radius
annotations.description: The disc-shaped radial head articulates with the capitulum and rotates within the annular ligament.

media.caption: Brachial plexus in anatomical context
media.attribution: Source: Gray's Anatomy: The Anatomical Basis of Clinical Practice. Educational reference from the local study library.

annotations.label: C5 root of brachial plexus
annotations.description: The C5 ventral ramus emerges between the anterior and middle scalene muscles and joins C6 to form the upper trunk of the brachial plexus.

annotations.label: C6 root of brachial plexus
annotations.description: The C6 ventral ramus passes through the interscalene interval and joins C5 to complete the upper trunk.

annotations.label: C7 root of brachial plexus
annotations.description: The C7 ventral ramus continues by itself as the middle trunk before dividing behind the clavicle.

annotations.label: C8 root of brachial plexus
annotations.description: The C8 ventral ramus ascends over the first rib to join T1 and form the lower trunk of the brachial plexus.

annotations.label: T1 root of brachial plexus
annotations.description: Most of the T1 ventral ramus joins C8 above the first rib to form the lower trunk; a smaller part remains as the first intercostal nerve.

annotations.label: Dorsal scapular nerve
annotations.description: A branch usually arising from the C5 root that pierces middle scalene and descends along the medial border of the scapula with the dorsal scapular artery.

annotations.label: Upper trunk of brachial plexus
annotations.description: The union of the C5 and C6 ventral rami at the lateral border of the scalene interval, dividing into anterior and posterior divisions above the clavicle.

annotations.label: Middle trunk of brachial plexus
annotations.description: The continuation of the C7 ventral ramus through the interscalene interval, dividing into anterior and posterior divisions behind the clavicle.

annotations.label: Lower trunk of brachial plexus
annotations.description: The union of C8 and T1 ventral rami, lying inferiorly in the plexus before dividing behind the clavicle.

annotations.label: Medial cord of brachial plexus
annotations.description: A cord medial to the second part of the axillary artery, formed by the anterior division of the lower trunk.

annotations.label: Lateral cord of brachial plexus
annotations.description: A cord lateral to the second part of the axillary artery, formed by the anterior divisions of the upper and middle trunks.

annotations.label: Posterior cord of brachial plexus
annotations.description: A cord posterior to the second part of the axillary artery, formed by all three posterior divisions.

annotations.label: Suprascapular nerve
annotations.description: A branch of the upper trunk that crosses the posterior triangle and passes under the superior transverse scapular ligament into the supraspinous fossa.

annotations.label: Lateral pectoral nerve
annotations.description: A branch of the lateral cord that crosses anterior to the axillary artery, pierces clavipectoral fascia and chiefly supplies pectoralis major.

annotations.label: Medial pectoral nerve
annotations.description: A branch of the medial cord that typically pierces pectoralis minor and continues into the deep surface of pectoralis major.

annotations.label: Axillary artery
annotations.description: The continuation of the subclavian from the lateral border of the first rib to the inferior border of teres major, where it becomes brachial.

annotations.label: Musculocutaneous nerve
annotations.description: A C5–C7 terminal branch of the lateral cord that pierces coracobrachialis and descends between biceps and brachialis before continuing as the lateral cutaneous nerve of the forearm.

annotations.label: Axillary nerve
annotations.description: A C5–C6 terminal branch of the posterior cord that passes through the quadrangular space with the posterior circumflex humeral artery and winds around the surgical neck.

annotations.label: Median nerve
annotations.description: A terminal nerve formed by lateral and medial roots around the axillary artery, descending with the brachial artery and entering the hand through the carpal tunnel.

annotations.label: Radial nerve
annotations.description: A large terminal branch of the posterior cord that passes through the triangular interval, winds in the radial groove and divides near the lateral elbow into superficial sensory and deep motor branches.

annotations.label: Ulnar nerve

annotations.label: Deltoid
annotations.description: A thick multipennate muscle forming the rounded shoulder, arising from the lateral clavicle, acromion and scapular spine and inserting on the deltoid tuberosity.

annotations.label: Coracobrachialis
annotations.description: Coracobrachialis runs from the coracoid process to the medial humeral shaft and is pierced by the musculocutaneous nerve.

annotations.label: Pectoralis major
annotations.description: Pectoralis major converges from the clavicle and anterior chest wall to the lateral lip of the intertubercular sulcus.

annotations.label: Serratus anterior
annotations.description: Serratus anterior attaches the lateral thoracic wall to the anterior surface of the medial scapular border.

annotations.label: Supraspinatus
annotations.description: A rotator-cuff muscle arising in the supraspinous fossa, passing beneath the acromion and inserting on the superior facet of the greater tubercle.

annotations.label: Subscapularis
annotations.description: A broad rotator-cuff muscle filling the subscapular fossa on the anterior scapula and inserting on the lesser tubercle of the humerus.

annotations.label: Teres major
annotations.description: Teres major passes from the inferior scapula to the medial lip of the intertubercular sulcus and contributes to the posterior axillary fold.

annotations.label: Coraco-acromial ligament
annotations.description: A strong triangular band from the coracoid process to the acromion that forms the roof of the coracoacromial arch above the humeral head.

annotations.label: Pectoralis minor
annotations.description: Pectoralis minor passes from the upper ribs to the coracoid process and forms part of the anterior wall of the axilla.

annotations.label: Subclavius
annotations.description: Subclavius lies below the clavicle and runs from the first rib and its costal cartilage to the inferior clavicular surface.

annotations.label: Clavicle
annotations.description: An S-shaped subcutaneous strut between the manubrium and acromion that holds the upper limb away from the trunk and transmits load to the axial skeleton.

annotations.label: Levator scapulae
annotations.description: Levator scapulae descends from upper cervical transverse processes to the upper medial border of the scapula.

annotations.label: Infraspinatus
annotations.description: A broad rotator-cuff muscle occupying the infraspinous fossa and inserting on the middle facet of the greater tubercle.

annotations.label: Teres minor
annotations.description: A narrow rotator-cuff muscle along the lateral scapular border that inserts on the inferior facet of the greater tubercle.

annotations.label: Latissimus dorsi
annotations.description: Latissimus dorsi passes from the back to the floor of the humeral intertubercular sulcus and forms part of the posterior axillary fold.

annotations.label: Trapezius
annotations.description: Trapezius attaches to the lateral clavicle, acromion and scapular spine and helps position and rotate the scapula.

annotations.label: Medial cutaneous nerve of forearm
annotations.description: A medial-cord sensory branch that descends with the basilic vein, pierces deep fascia in the arm and divides into anterior and posterior branches for the medial forearm.

annotations.label: Suprascapular nerve
annotations.description: A branch of the upper trunk that crosses the posterior triangle and passes under the superior transverse scapular ligament into the supraspinous fossa.

annotations.label: Brachial vein
annotations.description: The deep brachial veins accompany the brachial artery in the arm and contribute to the axillary venous drainage.

annotations.label: Deltoid
annotations.description: A thick multipennate muscle forming the rounded shoulder, arising from the lateral clavicle, acromion and scapular spine and inserting on the deltoid tuberosity.

annotations.label: Pectoralis minor
annotations.description: Pectoralis minor passes from the upper ribs to the coracoid process and forms part of the anterior wall of the axilla.

annotations.label: Lateral cord of brachial plexus
annotations.description: A cord lateral to the second part of the axillary artery, formed by the anterior divisions of the upper and middle trunks.

annotations.label: Axillary artery
annotations.description: The continuation of the subclavian from the lateral border of the first rib to the inferior border of teres major, where it becomes brachial.

annotations.label: Coracobrachialis
annotations.description: Coracobrachialis runs from the coracoid process to the medial humeral shaft and is pierced by the musculocutaneous nerve.

annotations.label: Musculocutaneous nerve
annotations.description: A C5–C7 terminal branch of the lateral cord that pierces coracobrachialis and descends between biceps and brachialis before continuing as the lateral cutaneous nerve of the forearm.

annotations.label: Biceps brachii, short and long heads
annotations.description: A two-headed anterior arm muscle whose long head arises from the supraglenoid tubercle and short head from the coracoid, joining to insert on the radial tuberosity and bicipital aponeurosis.

annotations.label: Median nerve
annotations.description: A terminal nerve formed by lateral and medial roots around the axillary artery, descending with the brachial artery and entering the hand through the carpal tunnel.

annotations.label: Brachial artery
annotations.description: The continuation of the axillary artery below teres major, running with the median nerve in the medial bicipital groove and dividing into radial and ulnar arteries in the cubital fossa.

annotations.label: Medial cord of brachial plexus
annotations.description: A cord medial to the second part of the axillary artery, formed by the anterior division of the lower trunk.

annotations.label: Posterior cord of brachial plexus
annotations.description: A cord posterior to the second part of the axillary artery, formed by all three posterior divisions.

annotations.label: Subscapularis
annotations.description: A broad rotator-cuff muscle filling the subscapular fossa on the anterior scapula and inserting on the lesser tubercle of the humerus.

annotations.label: Thoracodorsal nerve
annotations.description: A posterior-cord branch that descends along the posterior axillary wall with the thoracodorsal vessels to reach latissimus dorsi.

annotations.label: Medial cutaneous nerve of arm
annotations.description: A small medial-cord branch that descends along the medial axillary and brachial vessels to supply skin of the medial arm.

annotations.label: Radial nerve
annotations.description: A large terminal branch of the posterior cord that passes through the triangular interval, winds in the radial groove and divides near the lateral elbow into superficial sensory and deep motor branches.

annotations.label: Profunda brachii artery
annotations.description: The profunda brachii artery accompanies the radial nerve through the posterior arm and supplies the triceps region.

annotations.label: Ulnar nerve
annotations.description: A C8–T1 dominant terminal branch of the medial cord that passes behind the medial epicondyle, between the heads of flexor carpi ulnaris and into the hand superficial to the flexor retinaculum in Guyon's canal.

annotations.label: Supinator
annotations.description: A deep proximal posterior forearm muscle wrapping around the upper radius from the lateral epicondyle, annular ligament and supinator crest of the ulna.

annotations.label: Radius
annotations.description: The lateral forearm bone in anatomical position, with a disc-shaped head proximally and a broad distal end that articulates with the scaphoid and lunate.

annotations.label: Extensor pollicis longus
annotations.description: A deep posterior forearm muscle whose tendon turns around Lister's tubercle and reaches the distal phalanx of the thumb.

annotations.label: Abductor pollicis longus
annotations.description: A deep posterior forearm muscle whose tendon crosses the radial wrist to the base of the first metacarpal.

annotations.label: Extensor pollicis brevis
annotations.description: A deep posterior forearm muscle whose tendon runs with abductor pollicis longus to the base of the proximal thumb phalanx.

annotations.label: Olecranon
annotations.description: The olecranon forms the posterior prominence of the elbow and receives the triceps tendon.

annotations.label: Lateral epicondyle
annotations.description: The lateral epicondyle projects from the distal humerus and gives origin to the common extensor tendon.

annotations.label: Anconeus
annotations.description: Anconeus spans the lateral epicondyle, olecranon and proximal posterior ulna, assisting elbow extension and stability.

annotations.label: Flexor carpi ulnaris
annotations.description: A superficial anterior forearm muscle with humeral and ulnar heads, inserting through the pisiform onto the hamate and fifth metacarpal.

annotations.label: Ulna
annotations.description: The medial forearm bone, whose olecranon and coronoid process form the trochlear notch around the humeral trochlea; its distal head is separated from the carpus by an articular disc.

annotations.label: Extensor indicis
annotations.description: A deep posterior forearm muscle with a tendon to the extensor expansion of the index finger alongside extensor digitorum.

annotations.label: Ilium
annotations.description: The ilium is the broad superior part of the hip bone, expanding above the acetabulum into the iliac wing.

annotations.label: Pubis
annotations.description: The pubis is the anteroinferior part of the hip bone and contributes to the acetabulum and obturator foramen.

annotations.label: Ischium
annotations.description: The ischium forms the posteroinferior part of the hip bone and bears the ischial tuberosity.

annotations.label: Femur
annotations.description: The femur is the long bone of the thigh, extending from the hip to the knee with a head, neck, trochanters, shaft, condyles, and epicondyles.

annotations.label: Patella
annotations.description: The patella is a sesamoid bone embedded in the quadriceps tendon anterior to the knee, with its apex continuing into the patellar ligament.

annotations.label: Tibia
annotations.description: The tibia is the large medial weight-bearing bone of the leg, articulating with the femur, fibula, and talus. Its proximal condyles form the tibial plateau and its distal projection is the medial malleolus.

annotations.label: Fibula
annotations.description: The fibula is the slender lateral bone of the leg, joined to the tibia proximally and distally; its distal end forms the lateral malleolus.

annotations.label: Talus
annotations.description: The talus receives the tibia and fibula at the ankle and transmits load to the calcaneus and navicular.

annotations.label: Navicular
annotations.description: The navicular lies between the talar head and the three cuneiforms on the medial side of the foot.

annotations.label: Medial cuneiform
annotations.description: The medial cuneiform lies between the navicular and the base of the first metatarsal.

annotations.label: Calcaneus
annotations.description: The calcaneus forms the heel, lies below the talus and articulates anteriorly with the cuboid.

annotations.label: Metatarsals
annotations.description: The metatarsals form the long bones between the tarsus and the proximal toe phalanges.

annotations.label: Phalanges
annotations.description: Four lateral toes each have proximal, middle, and distal phalanges, whereas the great toe has only proximal and distal phalanges.

media.attribution: Source: Gray's Anatomy: The Anatomical Basis of Clinical Practice. Educational reference from the local study library.

annotations.label: Psoas major
annotations.description: Psoas major descends beside the lumbar spine and joins iliacus before inserting at the lesser trochanter.

annotations.label: Iliacus
annotations.description: Iliacus occupies the iliac fossa and joins the psoas tendon as the iliopsoas approaches the lesser trochanter.

annotations.label: Anterior superior iliac spine
annotations.description: The anterior superior iliac spine is the anterior end of the iliac crest and anchors sartorius and the inguinal ligament.

annotations.label: Inguinal ligament
annotations.description: The inguinal ligament spans the anterior superior iliac spine and pubic tubercle, forming the superior boundary of the femoral triangle.

annotations.label: Piriformis
annotations.description: A deep gluteal muscle leaving the pelvis through the greater sciatic foramen to insert on the superior greater trochanter.

annotations.label: Pectineus
annotations.description: A short flat muscle in the floor of the femoral triangle running from the superior pubic ramus to the pectineal line of the femur.

annotations.label: Tensor fasciae latae
annotations.description: A small anterolateral gluteal muscle from the anterior iliac crest and ASIS that inserts into the iliotibial tract.

annotations.label: Adductor longus
annotations.description: Adductor longus is a superficial triangular medial-thigh muscle running from the pubis to the middle third of the linea aspera.

annotations.label: Gracilis
annotations.description: Gracilis is a long superficial medial-thigh muscle running from the pubis to the medial proximal tibia in the pes anserinus.

annotations.label: Sartorius
annotations.description: A long strap muscle crossing from the ASIS obliquely over the anterior thigh to the upper medial tibia in the pes anserinus.

annotations.label: Rectus femoris
annotations.description: Rectus femoris is the superficial anterior component of quadriceps and crosses both the hip and knee joints.

annotations.label: Adductor magnus
annotations.description: This large medial-thigh muscle has an adductor part from the ischiopubic ramus and a hamstring part from the ischial tuberosity, inserting along the linea aspera and at the adductor tubercle.

annotations.label: Vastus lateralis
annotations.description: Vastus lateralis occupies the lateral thigh and contributes to the quadriceps tendon.

annotations.label: Vastus medialis
annotations.description: Vastus medialis occupies the medial anterior thigh and contributes to the quadriceps tendon and medial patellar support.

annotations.label: Iliotibial tract
annotations.description: The iliotibial tract is a thickened lateral portion of fascia lata that receives tensor fasciae latae and gluteus maximus.

annotations.label: Medial femoral circumflex artery
annotations.description: The medial circumflex femoral artery passes toward the posterior proximal femur and contributes the principal retinacular supply to the adult femoral head.

annotations.label: Common fibular nerve
annotations.description: This terminal branch of the sciatic nerve follows the biceps femoris tendon and winds around the fibular neck before dividing into superficial and deep fibular nerves.

annotations.label: Small saphenous vein
annotations.description: The small saphenous vein begins laterally in the dorsal venous arch, passes posterior to the lateral malleolus, and ascends the posterior calf to drain into the popliteal vein.

annotations.label: Gluteus medius
annotations.description: Gluteus medius lies deep to gluteus maximus on the lateral ilium and inserts on the greater trochanter.

annotations.label: Iliac crest
annotations.description: The iliac crest is the curved superior margin of the ilium.

annotations.label: Gluteus maximus
annotations.description: This large superficial gluteal muscle passes from the posterior ilium, sacrum, and coccyx to the iliotibial tract and gluteal tuberosity.

annotations.label: Gemellus superior
annotations.description: A small deep gluteal muscle from the ischial spine that joins the superior surface of the obturator internus tendon.

annotations.label: Gemellus inferior
annotations.description: A small deep gluteal muscle from the ischial tuberosity that joins the inferior surface of the obturator internus tendon.

annotations.label: Obturator internus
annotations.description: A lateral rotator arising inside the pelvis whose tendon turns through the lesser sciatic foramen to the medial greater trochanter.

annotations.label: Posterior femoral cutaneous nerve
annotations.description: A sacral-plexus sensory nerve that exits inferior to piriformis, descends deep to fascia lata and supplies the posterior thigh.

annotations.label: Greater trochanter of femur
annotations.description: The greater trochanter is the large lateral prominence of the proximal femur and receives gluteal and short lateral rotator attachments.

annotations.label: Gluteus minimus
annotations.description: Gluteus minimus is the deepest gluteal muscle, passing from the lateral ilium to the anterior greater trochanter.

annotations.label: Gracilis
annotations.description: Gracilis is a long superficial medial-thigh muscle running from the pubis to the medial proximal tibia in the pes anserinus.

annotations.label: Tensor fasciae latae
annotations.description: A small anterolateral gluteal muscle from the anterior iliac crest and ASIS that inserts into the iliotibial tract.

annotations.label: Nerve to obturator internus
annotations.description: A sacral-plexus branch that exits below piriformis, hooks around the ischial spine and enters the lesser sciatic foramen to reach obturator internus.

annotations.label: Piriformis
annotations.description: A deep gluteal muscle leaving the pelvis through the greater sciatic foramen to insert on the superior greater trochanter.

annotations.label: Sciatic nerve
annotations.description: The sciatic nerve leaves the pelvis through the greater sciatic foramen, usually inferior to piriformis, and descends in the posterior thigh before dividing into tibial and common fibular nerves.

annotations.label: Quadratus femoris
annotations.description: A flat rectangular deep gluteal muscle spanning the lateral ischial tuberosity to the quadrate tubercle of the femur.

annotations.label: Adductor magnus
annotations.description: This large medial-thigh muscle has an adductor part from the ischiopubic ramus and a hamstring part from the ischial tuberosity, inserting along the linea aspera and at the adductor tubercle.

annotations.label: Ischial tuberosity
annotations.description: The ischial tuberosity is the weight-bearing prominence of the inferior ischium and an origin for the hamstrings.

annotations.label: Tibial nerve
annotations.description: The tibial component of the sciatic nerve descends through the popliteal fossa and posterior leg, then passes behind the medial malleolus into the sole.

annotations.label: Plantaris
annotations.description: A small posterior-leg muscle with a short belly above the knee and a very long slender tendon descending toward the calcaneus.

annotations.label: Semimembranosus
annotations.description: Semimembranosus lies deep to semitendinosus and passes from the ischial tuberosity to the posterior medial tibial condyle.

annotations.label: Adductor hiatus
annotations.description: The adductor hiatus is the opening in distal adductor magnus through which the femoral vessels pass to the popliteal fossa.

annotations.label: Semitendinosus (retracted)
annotations.description: Semitendinosus descends from the ischial tuberosity to the upper medial tibia as part of the pes anserinus.

annotations.label: Semitendinosus
annotations.description: Semitendinosus descends from the ischial tuberosity to the upper medial tibia as part of the pes anserinus.

annotations.label: Semimembranosus
annotations.description: Semimembranosus lies deep to semitendinosus and passes from the ischial tuberosity to the posterior medial tibial condyle.

annotations.label: Popliteal vein
annotations.description: The popliteal vein is formed by deep veins of the leg, lies superficial to the popliteal artery in the fossa, and becomes the femoral vein at the adductor hiatus.

annotations.label: Popliteal artery
annotations.description: The popliteal artery is the continuation of the femoral artery behind the knee and lies deepest in the popliteal fossa against the capsule and femur.

annotations.label: Patella
annotations.description: The patella is a sesamoid bone embedded in the quadriceps tendon anterior to the knee, with its apex continuing into the patellar ligament.

annotations.label: Iliotibial tract
annotations.description: The iliotibial tract is a thickened lateral portion of fascia lata that receives tensor fasciae latae and gluteus maximus.

annotations.label: Patellar ligament
annotations.description: The patellar ligament connects the apex of the patella to the tibial tuberosity as the distal continuation of the knee extensor mechanism.

annotations.label: Fibularis longus
annotations.description: Fibularis longus occupies the lateral leg, then passes behind the lateral malleolus and beneath the foot toward the first metatarsal and medial cuneiform.

annotations.label: Tibialis anterior
annotations.description: This superficial anterior-compartment muscle runs from the lateral tibia to the medial cuneiform and base of the first metatarsal.

annotations.label: Extensor digitorum longus
annotations.description: This anterior-compartment muscle descends to four tendons for the lateral four toes.

annotations.label: Fibularis brevis
annotations.description: Fibularis brevis lies deep to fibularis longus and inserts on the tuberosity at the base of the fifth metatarsal.

annotations.label: Extensor hallucis longus
annotations.description: A deep anterior-leg muscle between tibialis anterior and extensor digitorum longus whose tendon reaches the distal hallux phalanx.

annotations.label: Lateral malleolus
annotations.description: The lateral malleolus is the distal fibular prominence on the lateral side of the ankle.

annotations.label: Extensor digitorum brevis
annotations.description: Extensor digitorum brevis lies on the dorsum of the foot and extends toes two through four.

annotations.label: Tibial tuberosity
annotations.description: The tibial tuberosity is the anterior proximal tibial prominence receiving the patellar ligament.

annotations.label: Gastrocnemius
annotations.description: The two-headed gastrocnemius arises above the femoral condyles and joins soleus in the calcaneal tendon.

annotations.label: Soleus
annotations.description: Soleus is the broad postural muscle deep to gastrocnemius, arising from the tibia and fibula and joining the calcaneal tendon.

annotations.label: Tibia
annotations.description: The tibia is the large medial weight-bearing bone of the leg, articulating with the femur, fibula, and talus. Its proximal condyles form the tibial plateau and its distal projection is the medial malleolus.

annotations.label: Medial malleolus
annotations.description: The medial malleolus is the distal tibial projection on the medial side of the ankle.

annotations.label: Extensor hallucis brevis
annotations.description: Extensor hallucis brevis is the medial short extensor on the dorsum of the foot and inserts into the hallux proximal phalanx.

annotations.label: Fibularis tertius
annotations.description: A variable anterior-compartment muscle, often continuous with extensor digitorum longus, inserting on the dorsal base of the fifth metatarsal.

annotations.label: Biceps femoris
annotations.description: The long and short heads form the lateral hamstring and insert mainly on the head of the fibula.

annotations.label: Head of fibula
annotations.description: The fibular head is the expanded proximal fibula and articulates with the lateral tibial condyle.

annotations.label: Calcaneal tendon
annotations.description: The calcaneal tendon combines the gastrocnemius and soleus tendons and inserts into the posterior calcaneus.

annotations.label: Metatarsals
annotations.description: Five metatarsals form the forefoot between the tarsals and proximal phalanges, each with a base, shaft, and head.

annotations.label: Phalanges
annotations.description: Four lateral toes each have proximal, middle, and distal phalanges, whereas the great toe has only proximal and distal phalanges.

annotations.label: Calcaneus
annotations.description: The calcaneus forms the heel, lies below the talus and articulates anteriorly with the cuboid.

annotations.label: Talus
annotations.description: The talus receives the tibia and fibula at the ankle and transmits load to the calcaneus and navicular.

annotations.label: Navicular
annotations.description: The navicular lies between the talar head and the three cuneiforms on the medial side of the foot.

annotations.label: Intermediate cuneiform
annotations.description: The intermediate cuneiform lies between the navicular and the second metatarsal, between the medial and lateral cuneiforms.

annotations.label: Lateral cuneiform
annotations.description: The lateral cuneiform lies anterior to the navicular and mainly articulates distally with the third metatarsal.

annotations.label: Fibular trochlea
annotations.description: The fibular trochlea is the lateral calcaneal prominence separating the courses of the fibularis brevis and longus tendons.

annotations.label: Cuboid
annotations.description: The cuboid lies in the lateral foot between the calcaneus and the fourth and fifth metatarsals.

annotations.label: Medial cuneiform
annotations.description: The medial cuneiform lies between the navicular and the base of the first metatarsal.

annotations.label: Posterior tibiofibular ligament
annotations.description: The posterior tibiofibular ligament strengthens the posterior part of the distal tibiofibular syndesmosis.

annotations.label: Lateral malleolus
annotations.description: The lateral malleolus is the distal fibular prominence on the lateral side of the ankle.

annotations.label: Posterior talofibular ligament
annotations.description: The posterior talofibular ligament links the lateral malleolus to the posterior talus as part of the lateral ankle ligament complex.

annotations.label: Calcaneofibular ligament
annotations.description: The calcaneofibular ligament runs from the lateral malleolus toward the lateral calcaneus.

annotations.label: Medial malleolus
annotations.description: The medial malleolus is the distal tibial projection on the medial side of the ankle.

annotations.label: Posterior process of talus
annotations.description: The posterior process of the talus lies behind the talar trochlea and is divided by the groove for flexor hallucis longus.

annotations.label: Talonavicular ligament
annotations.description: The dorsal talonavicular ligament reinforces the talonavicular joint between the talar neck and navicular.

annotations.label: Tuberosity of navicular
annotations.description: The navicular tuberosity projects medially and receives the main tibialis posterior tendon attachment.

annotations.label: Long plantar ligament
annotations.description: The long plantar ligament runs from the plantar calcaneus toward the cuboid and metatarsal bases, supporting the lateral longitudinal arch.

annotations.label: Plantar calcaneonavicular (spring) ligament
annotations.description: The spring ligament spans the sustentaculum tali and navicular and supports the head of the talus.

annotations.label: Sustentaculum tali
annotations.description: The sustentaculum tali is the medial calcaneal shelf supporting the talus.

annotations.label: Superficial parts of deltoid ligament
annotations.description: The superficial deltoid ligament fans from the medial malleolus toward the navicular, calcaneus and talus, reinforcing the medial ankle.

annotations.label: Anterior tibiofibular ligament
annotations.description: The anterior tibiofibular ligament strengthens the front of the distal tibiofibular syndesmosis.

annotations.label: Anterior talofibular ligament
annotations.description: The anterior talofibular ligament links the anterior lateral malleolus to the talar neck.

annotations.label: Bifurcate ligament
annotations.description: The bifurcate ligament arises from the anterior calcaneus and divides toward the navicular and cuboid.

annotations.label: Common plantar digital nerves
annotations.description: The common plantar digital nerves run forward in the sole and divide into proper digital branches for adjacent toes.

annotations.label: Lateral plantar artery
annotations.description: The larger terminal branch of the posterior tibial artery that crosses the lateral sole and turns medially to form most of the deep plantar arch.

annotations.label: Abductor digiti minimi
annotations.description: In the foot, abductor digiti minimi occupies the lateral sole and inserts on the lateral side of the fifth toe proximal phalanx.

annotations.label: Plantar aponeurosis
annotations.description: The plantar aponeurosis runs from the calcaneal tuberosity toward the toes and supports the longitudinal arch.

annotations.label: Lateral plantar nerve
annotations.description: The smaller tibial terminal branch runs obliquely across the sole with the lateral plantar artery and divides into superficial and deep branches.

annotations.label: Posterior tibial artery
annotations.description: This terminal branch of the popliteal artery descends in the deep posterior compartment and passes behind the medial malleolus into the sole.

annotations.label: Flexor retinaculum
annotations.description: The ankle flexor retinaculum extends from the medial malleolus to the calcaneus and roofs the tarsal tunnel.

annotations.label: Medial plantar nerve
annotations.description: The larger tibial terminal branch runs forward in the sole with the medial plantar artery between abductor hallucis and flexor digitorum brevis.

annotations.label: Flexor accessorius
annotations.description: Flexor accessorius, also called quadratus plantae, arises from the calcaneus and joins the flexor digitorum longus tendons.

annotations.label: Abductor hallucis
annotations.description: Abductor hallucis occupies the medial margin of the sole and inserts on the medial side of the hallux proximal phalanx.

annotations.label: Flexor hallucis brevis
annotations.description: Flexor hallucis brevis is a short plantar muscle whose two heads insert on either side of the base of the hallux proximal phalanx.

annotations.label: Flexor digitorum brevis
annotations.description: Flexor digitorum brevis lies in the first plantar muscle layer and sends divided tendons to the middle phalanges of toes two through five.

annotations.label: Lateral plantar artery
annotations.description: The larger terminal branch of the posterior tibial artery that crosses the lateral sole and turns medially to form most of the deep plantar arch.

annotations.label: Abductor digiti minimi

annotations.label: Plantar aponeurosis
annotations.description: The plantar aponeurosis runs from the calcaneal tuberosity toward the toes and supports the longitudinal arch.

annotations.label: Lateral plantar nerve
annotations.description: The smaller tibial terminal branch runs obliquely across the sole with the lateral plantar artery and divides into superficial and deep branches.

annotations.label: Posterior tibial artery
annotations.description: This terminal branch of the popliteal artery descends in the deep posterior compartment and passes behind the medial malleolus into the sole.

annotations.label: Flexor retinaculum
annotations.description: The ankle flexor retinaculum extends from the medial malleolus to the calcaneus and roofs the tarsal tunnel.

annotations.label: Medial plantar nerve

annotations.label: Flexor digitorum brevis

annotations.label: Nasal bone
annotations.description: The nasal bone forms the bony bridge above the lateral nasal cartilage.

annotations.label: Lateral nasal cartilage
annotations.description: The lateral nasal cartilage lies below the nasal bone in the external nasal skeleton.

annotations.label: Septal cartilage
annotations.description: The septal cartilage forms the anterior cartilaginous part of the nasal septum.

annotations.label: Vomer
annotations.description: The vomer forms the posteroinferior part of the bony nasal septum.

annotations.label: Sphenoidal sinus
annotations.description: The sphenoidal sinus occupies the body of the sphenoid posterior to the nasal cavity.

annotations.label: Superior nasal concha
annotations.description: The superior concha is the upper ethmoidal projection on the lateral nasal wall.

annotations.label: Middle nasal concha
annotations.description: The middle concha is an ethmoidal projection below the superior concha.

annotations.label: Inferior nasal concha
annotations.description: The inferior concha is a separate bone forming the lowest concha.

annotations.label: Perpendicular plate of ethmoid
annotations.description: The perpendicular plate of the ethmoid forms the superior part of the bony nasal septum.

annotations.label: Major alar cartilage
annotations.description: The major alar cartilage supports the mobile lower portion of the external nose.

annotations.label: Posterior cricoarytenoid muscle
annotations.description: Posterior cricoarytenoid abducts the vocal folds by rotating the arytenoid cartilages.

annotations.label: Lateral cricoarytenoid muscle
annotations.description: Lateral cricoarytenoid rotates the arytenoid to adduct the vocal fold.

annotations.label: Transverse arytenoid muscle
annotations.description: The transverse interarytenoid muscle draws the arytenoid cartilages together.

annotations.label: Oblique arytenoid muscle
annotations.description: The oblique arytenoid muscles cross between the arytenoids and help narrow the laryngeal inlet.

annotations.label: Thyroarytenoid muscle
annotations.description: Thyroarytenoid shortens the vocal fold by drawing the arytenoid toward the thyroid cartilage.

annotations.label: Vocalis muscle
annotations.description: Vocalis lies alongside the vocal ligament and adjusts its local tension.

annotations.label: Cricothyroid muscle
annotations.description: Cricothyroid tilts the thyroid relative to the cricoid and increases vocal fold tension.

annotations.label: Vocal ligament
annotations.description: The vocal ligament extends from the thyroid cartilage to the arytenoid vocal process.

annotations.label: Thyroid cartilage
annotations.description: The thyroid cartilage provides the anterior attachment for the vocal ligament and intrinsic muscles.

annotations.label: Cricoid cartilage
annotations.description: The cricoid supports the arytenoids and gives origin to the cricoarytenoid muscles.

annotations.label: Arytenoid cartilage
annotations.description: The arytenoid rotates and glides at the cricoarytenoid joint to move the vocal fold.

annotations.label: Cricoid cartilage
annotations.description: The cricoid cartilage forms the complete ring below the thyroid cartilage.

annotations.label: Trachea
annotations.description: The trachea continues inferiorly from the larynx below the cricoid cartilage.

annotations.label: Superior vena cava
annotations.description: The superior vena cava descends on the right side of the superior mediastinum and opens into the superior aspect of the right atrium.

annotations.label: Arch of aorta
annotations.description: The aortic arch curves superiorly and posteriorly over the root of the left lung and gives rise to the great arteries supplying the head, neck and upper limbs.

annotations.label: Right auricle
annotations.description: The right auricle is the muscular appendage of the right atrium that overlaps the root of the ascending aorta.

annotations.label: Right atrium
annotations.description: The right atrium receives the superior vena cava, inferior vena cava and coronary sinus and opens into the right ventricle through the tricuspid valve.

annotations.label: Pulmonary trunk
annotations.description: The pulmonary trunk leaves the right ventricle and divides into the right and left pulmonary arteries.

annotations.label: Left auricle
annotations.description: The left auricle is the muscular appendage of the left atrium that projects beside the pulmonary trunk.

annotations.label: Pulmonary valve
annotations.description: The pulmonary valve guards the outflow of the right ventricle into the pulmonary trunk and has three semilunar leaflets.

annotations.label: Conus arteriosus
annotations.description: The conus arteriosus is the smooth outflow region of the right ventricle leading to the pulmonary valve.

annotations.label: Septal papillary muscle
annotations.description: The septal papillary muscle belongs to the right ventricular tricuspid apparatus and attaches chordae to valve leaflets.

annotations.label: Septomarginal trabecula
annotations.description: The septomarginal trabecula, or moderator band, crosses the right ventricular cavity from the septum toward the anterior papillary muscle.

annotations.label: Tricuspid valve
annotations.description: The tricuspid valve guards the right atrioventricular opening. Its leaflets connect by chordae tendineae to right ventricular papillary muscles.

annotations.label: Chordae tendineae
annotations.description: These tendinous cords connect atrioventricular valve leaflets to papillary muscles and help prevent leaflet prolapse during ventricular contraction.

annotations.label: Anterior papillary muscle
annotations.description: The anterior papillary muscle shown here belongs to the right ventricle and anchors tricuspid valve leaflets through chordae tendineae.

annotations.label: Posterior papillary muscle
annotations.description: The posterior papillary muscle shown here belongs to the right ventricle and anchors tricuspid valve leaflets through chordae tendineae.

annotations.label: Trabeculae carneae
annotations.description: Trabeculae carneae are the irregular muscular ridges of the ventricular wall, contrasting with the smoother ventricular outflow tracts.

annotations.label: Superior vena cava
annotations.description: The superior vena cava descends on the right side of the superior mediastinum and opens into the superior aspect of the right atrium.

annotations.label: Arch of aorta
annotations.description: The aortic arch curves superiorly and posteriorly over the root of the left lung and gives rise to the great arteries supplying the head, neck and upper limbs.

annotations.label: Right auricle
annotations.description: The right auricle is the muscular appendage of the right atrium that overlaps the root of the ascending aorta.

annotations.label: Right atrium
annotations.description: The right atrium receives the superior vena cava, inferior vena cava and coronary sinus and opens into the right ventricle through the tricuspid valve.

annotations.label: Pulmonary trunk
annotations.description: The pulmonary trunk leaves the right ventricle and divides into the right and left pulmonary arteries.

annotations.label: Left auricle
annotations.description: The left auricle is the muscular appendage of the left atrium that projects beside the pulmonary trunk.

annotations.label: Pulmonary valve
annotations.description: The pulmonary valve guards the outflow of the right ventricle into the pulmonary trunk and has three semilunar leaflets.

annotations.label: Conus arteriosus
annotations.description: The conus arteriosus is the smooth outflow region of the right ventricle leading to the pulmonary valve.

annotations.label: Septal papillary muscle
annotations.description: The septal papillary muscle belongs to the right ventricular tricuspid apparatus and attaches chordae to valve leaflets.

annotations.label: Septomarginal trabecula
annotations.description: The septomarginal trabecula, or moderator band, crosses the right ventricular cavity from the septum toward the anterior papillary muscle.

annotations.label: Tricuspid valve
annotations.description: The tricuspid valve guards the right atrioventricular opening. Its leaflets connect by chordae tendineae to right ventricular papillary muscles.

annotations.label: Chordae tendineae
annotations.description: These tendinous cords connect atrioventricular valve leaflets to papillary muscles and help prevent leaflet prolapse during ventricular contraction.

annotations.label: Anterior papillary muscle
annotations.description: The anterior papillary muscle shown here belongs to the right ventricle and anchors tricuspid valve leaflets through chordae tendineae.

annotations.label: Posterior papillary muscle
annotations.description: The posterior papillary muscle shown here belongs to the right ventricle and anchors tricuspid valve leaflets through chordae tendineae.

annotations.label: Trabeculae carneae
annotations.description: Trabeculae carneae are the irregular muscular ridges of the ventricular wall, contrasting with the smoother ventricular outflow tracts.

annotations.description: The anterior, or aortic, leaflet of the mitral valve lies adjacent to the aortic outlet and attaches to chordae tendineae from the ventricular papillary muscles.

annotations.label: Chordae tendineae
annotations.description: These tendinous cords connect atrioventricular valve leaflets to papillary muscles and help prevent leaflet prolapse during ventricular contraction.

annotations.label: Anterior papillary muscle
annotations.description: The anterior papillary muscle shown here belongs to the left ventricle and anchors mitral valve leaflets through chordae tendineae.

annotations.label: Trabeculae carneae
annotations.description: Trabeculae carneae are the irregular muscular ridges of the ventricular wall, contrasting with the smoother ventricular outflow tracts.

annotations.label: Posterior papillary muscle

annotations.label: Posterior cusp of mitral valve

annotations.description: The left atrium receives the pulmonary veins and forms most of the posterior base of the heart.

annotations.description: The coronary sinus occupies the posterior atrioventricular groove and receives major cardiac veins before opening into the right atrium.

annotations.label: Pulmonary veins

annotations.label: Arch of aorta
annotations.description: The aortic arch curves superiorly and posteriorly over the root of the left lung and gives rise to the great arteries supplying the head, neck and upper limbs.

annotations.label: Anterior cusp of mitral valve
annotations.description: The anterior, or aortic, leaflet of the mitral valve lies adjacent to the aortic outlet and attaches to chordae tendineae from the ventricular papillary muscles.

annotations.label: Chordae tendineae
annotations.description: These tendinous cords connect atrioventricular valve leaflets to papillary muscles and help prevent leaflet prolapse during ventricular contraction.

annotations.label: Anterior papillary muscle
annotations.description: The anterior papillary muscle shown here belongs to the left ventricle and anchors mitral valve leaflets through chordae tendineae.

annotations.label: Trabeculae carneae
annotations.description: Trabeculae carneae are the irregular muscular ridges of the ventricular wall, contrasting with the smoother ventricular outflow tracts.

annotations.label: Posterior papillary muscle
annotations.description: The posterior papillary muscle shown here belongs to the left ventricle and anchors mitral valve leaflets through chordae tendineae.

annotations.label: Posterior cusp of mitral valve
annotations.description: The posterior, or mural, leaflet of the mitral valve borders the posterior part of the left atrioventricular opening and attaches to chordae tendineae.

annotations.label: Left atrium
annotations.description: The left atrium receives the pulmonary veins and forms most of the posterior base of the heart.

annotations.label: Coronary sinus
annotations.description: The coronary sinus occupies the posterior atrioventricular groove and receives major cardiac veins before opening into the right atrium.

annotations.label: Pulmonary veins
annotations.description: The pulmonary veins convey oxygenated blood from the lungs into the left atrium.

media.alt: Surface features of a typical rib. Internal aspect with detail of posterior end. Original source diagram with leader lines.
media.caption: Surface features of a typical rib
media.attribution: Source: Cardiovascular anatomy lecture: Bones 3, slide 10. Educational reference from the local study library.

annotations.label: Head of rib
annotations.description: The head forms the posterior vertebral end of a rib. A typical head bears two facets for articulation with adjacent vertebral bodies.

annotations.label: Tubercle of rib
annotations.description: The rib tubercle lies at the junction of the neck and shaft and includes articular and non-articular parts.

annotations.label: Angle of rib
annotations.description: The angle is the point of greatest curvature of the rib, lateral to its tubercle.

annotations.label: Neck of rib
annotations.description: The neck is the short segment between the rib head and tubercle.

annotations.label: Internal surface of rib
annotations.description: The internal surface is the concave surface facing the thoracic cavity and includes the costal groove near its inferior border.

annotations.label: Costal groove
annotations.description: The costal groove runs along the internal surface near the inferior border of a rib and shelters the main intercostal neurovascular bundle.

annotations.label: Costal cartilage
annotations.description: Costal cartilage continues the anterior end of a rib and contributes to the flexible anterior thoracic wall.

annotations.label: External surface of rib
annotations.description: The external surface is the convex surface of the rib facing away from the thoracic cavity.

annotations.label: Crest of head of rib
annotations.description: The crest separates the two articular facets on the head of a typical rib and provides attachment for the intra-articular ligament.

annotations.label: Articular facets of head of rib
annotations.description: A typical rib head has two articular facets separated by a crest. These facets articulate with the bodies of adjacent thoracic vertebrae.

annotations.label: Articular facet of tubercle
annotations.description: The smooth articular part of the rib tubercle meets the transverse costal facet of the corresponding thoracic vertebra.

annotations.label: Non-articular part of tubercle
annotations.description: The rough non-articular part of the rib tubercle provides attachment for the lateral costotransverse ligament.

annotations.label: Head of rib
annotations.description: The head forms the posterior vertebral end of a rib. A typical head bears two facets for articulation with adjacent vertebral bodies.

annotations.label: Tubercle of rib
annotations.description: The rib tubercle lies at the junction of the neck and shaft and includes articular and non-articular parts.

annotations.label: Angle of rib
annotations.description: The angle is the point of greatest curvature of the rib, lateral to its tubercle.

annotations.label: Neck of rib
annotations.description: The neck is the short segment between the rib head and tubercle.

annotations.label: Internal surface of rib
annotations.description: The internal surface is the concave surface facing the thoracic cavity and includes the costal groove near its inferior border.

annotations.label: Costal groove
annotations.description: The costal groove runs along the internal surface near the inferior border of a rib and shelters the main intercostal neurovascular bundle.

annotations.label: Costal cartilage
annotations.description: Costal cartilage continues the anterior end of a rib and contributes to the flexible anterior thoracic wall.

annotations.label: External surface of rib
annotations.description: The external surface is the convex surface of the rib facing away from the thoracic cavity.

annotations.label: Crest of head of rib
annotations.description: The crest separates the two articular facets on the head of a typical rib and provides attachment for the intra-articular ligament.

annotations.label: Articular facets of head of rib
annotations.description: A typical rib head has two articular facets separated by a crest. These facets articulate with the bodies of adjacent thoracic vertebrae.

annotations.label: Articular facet of tubercle
annotations.description: The smooth articular part of the rib tubercle meets the transverse costal facet of the corresponding thoracic vertebra.

annotations.label: Non-articular part of tubercle
annotations.description: The rough non-articular part of the rib tubercle provides attachment for the lateral costotransverse ligament.

annotations.label: Lesser splanchnic nerve
annotations.description: The lesser thoracic splanchnic nerve descends from the lower thoracic sympathetic trunk, below the greater splanchnic nerve, toward abdominal autonomic plexuses.

annotations.label: Least splanchnic nerve
annotations.description: The least thoracic splanchnic nerve is the lowest of the three labeled splanchnic nerves and descends from the lower thoracic sympathetic trunk toward the abdomen.

annotations.label: Greater splanchnic nerve

annotations.label: Lesser splanchnic nerve

annotations.label: Least splanchnic nerve
annotations.description: The least thoracic splanchnic nerve is the lowest of the three labeled splanchnic nerves and descends from the lower thoracic sympathetic trunk toward the abdomen.

annotations.label: Left common carotid artery
annotations.description: The left common carotid artery arises directly from the aortic arch and ascends into the neck.

annotations.label: Superior mediastinum
annotations.description: The superior mediastinum lies above the transverse thoracic plane and contains the aortic arch, major veins, trachea and oesophagus.

annotations.label: Thymus
annotations.description: The thymus lies behind the sternum, occupying the anterior part of the superior mediastinum and extending variably into the anterior mediastinum.

annotations.label: Manubrium
annotations.description: The manubrium forms the superior part of the sternum and joins the sternal body at the sternal angle.

annotations.label: Sternal angle
annotations.description: The sternal angle marks the junction of the manubrium and body and is an anterior landmark for the transverse thoracic plane.

annotations.label: Anterior mediastinum
annotations.description: The anterior mediastinum lies between the sternum and the pericardium below the transverse thoracic plane.

annotations.label: Middle mediastinum
annotations.description: The middle mediastinum contains the heart and pericardium together with the roots of the great vessels.

annotations.label: Diaphragm
annotations.description: The diaphragm forms the muscular partition between thorax and abdomen and closes the inferior thoracic aperture.

annotations.label: Inferior vena cava
annotations.description: The inferior vena cava passes through the diaphragm and enters the inferior aspect of the right atrium.

annotations.label: Posterior mediastinum
annotations.description: The posterior mediastinum lies behind the pericardium and contains the oesophagus, descending thoracic aorta, azygos system and thoracic duct.

annotations.label: Trachea
annotations.description: The trachea descends in front of the oesophagus and divides into the right and left main bronchi.

annotations.label: Left subclavian artery
annotations.description: The left subclavian artery is the third usual branch of the aortic arch and travels toward the root of the neck and upper limb.

annotations.label: Arch of aorta
annotations.description: The aortic arch curves superiorly and posteriorly over the root of the left lung and gives rise to the great arteries supplying the head, neck and upper limbs.

annotations.label: Right pulmonary artery
annotations.description: The right pulmonary artery passes toward the right lung behind the ascending aorta and superior vena cava.

annotations.label: Left main bronchus
annotations.description: The left main bronchus passes below the aortic arch toward the root of the left lung.

annotations.label: Descending thoracic aorta
annotations.description: The descending thoracic aorta runs through the posterior mediastinum to the left of the vertebral column before passing through the diaphragm.

annotations.label: Oesophagus
annotations.description: The oesophagus lies posterior to the trachea and continues through the posterior mediastinum toward the diaphragm.

annotations.label: Common plantar digital nerves
annotations.description: The common plantar digital nerves run forward in the sole and divide into proper digital branches for adjacent toes.

annotations.label: Lateral plantar artery
annotations.description: The larger terminal branch of the posterior tibial artery that crosses the lateral sole and turns medially to form most of the deep plantar arch.

annotations.label: Abductor digiti minimi
annotations.description: In the foot, abductor digiti minimi occupies the lateral sole and inserts on the lateral side of the fifth toe proximal phalanx.

annotations.label: Plantar aponeurosis
annotations.description: The plantar aponeurosis runs from the calcaneal tuberosity toward the toes and supports the longitudinal arch.

annotations.label: Lateral plantar nerve
annotations.description: The smaller tibial terminal branch runs obliquely across the sole with the lateral plantar artery and divides into superficial and deep branches.

annotations.label: Posterior tibial artery
annotations.description: This terminal branch of the popliteal artery descends in the deep posterior compartment and passes behind the medial malleolus into the sole.

annotations.label: Flexor retinaculum
annotations.description: The ankle flexor retinaculum extends from the medial malleolus to the calcaneus and roofs the tarsal tunnel.

annotations.label: Medial plantar nerve
annotations.description: The larger tibial terminal branch runs forward in the sole with the medial plantar artery between abductor hallucis and flexor digitorum brevis.

annotations.label: Flexor accessorius
annotations.description: Flexor accessorius, also called quadratus plantae, arises from the calcaneus and joins the flexor digitorum longus tendons.

annotations.label: Abductor hallucis
annotations.description: Abductor hallucis occupies the medial margin of the sole and inserts on the medial side of the hallux proximal phalanx.

annotations.label: Flexor hallucis brevis
annotations.description: Flexor hallucis brevis is a short plantar muscle whose two heads insert on either side of the base of the hallux proximal phalanx.

annotations.label: Flexor digitorum brevis
annotations.description: Flexor digitorum brevis lies in the first plantar muscle layer and sends divided tendons to the middle phalanges of toes two through five.

annotations.label: Nasal septum
annotations.description: The nasal septum is the median wall separating the right and left nasal cavities.

annotations.label: Nasopharynx
annotations.description: The nasopharynx lies behind the choanae and above the soft palate; it occupies the superior green space.

annotations.label: Oropharynx
annotations.description: The oropharynx lies posterior to the oral cavity and inferior to the soft palate; it occupies the lower green space.

annotations.label: Soft palate
annotations.description: The soft palate is the movable posterior continuation of the hard palate; it forms the boundary below the nasopharynx.

annotations.label: Nares
annotations.description: The nares are the anterior openings of the nasal cavities on the inferior surface of the external nose.

annotations.label: Oral cavity
annotations.description: The oral cavity lies inferior to the nasal cavities and anterior to the oropharynx; it is represented by the pink space.

annotations.label: Epiglottis
annotations.description: The epiglottis is the leaf-shaped cartilage forming the anterior boundary of the laryngeal inlet.

annotations.label: Aryepiglottic fold
annotations.description: An aryepiglottic fold forms a lateral border of the laryngeal inlet and encloses the upper margin of the quadrangular membrane.

annotations.label: Cuneiform tubercle
annotations.description: This mucosal prominence overlies a cuneiform cartilage in the aryepiglottic fold, anterior to the corniculate prominence.

annotations.label: Corniculate tubercle
annotations.description: This prominence overlies a corniculate cartilage at the apex of an arytenoid, posterior to the cuneiform prominence.

annotations.label: Oblique arytenoid muscle
annotations.description: The paired oblique arytenoids cross between opposite arytenoid cartilages and help narrow the laryngeal inlet.

annotations.label: Transverse arytenoid muscle
annotations.description: The unpaired transverse arytenoid runs horizontally between the arytenoid cartilages and adducts them.

annotations.label: Posterior crico-arytenoid muscle
annotations.description: This muscle arises from the posterior cricoid lamina and inserts on the arytenoid muscular process; it abducts the vocal fold.

annotations.label: Cricoid cartilage
annotations.description: The broad posterior cricoid lamina supports the posterior crico-arytenoid muscles; its exposed cartilaginous edges are pale blue-gray.

annotations.label: Epiglottis
annotations.description: The epiglottis is the leaf-shaped cartilage forming the anterior boundary of the laryngeal inlet.

annotations.label: Aryepiglottic fold
annotations.description: An aryepiglottic fold forms a lateral border of the laryngeal inlet and encloses the upper margin of the quadrangular membrane.

annotations.label: Cuneiform tubercle
annotations.description: This mucosal prominence overlies a cuneiform cartilage in the aryepiglottic fold, anterior to the corniculate prominence.

annotations.label: Corniculate tubercle
annotations.description: This prominence overlies a corniculate cartilage at the apex of an arytenoid, posterior to the cuneiform prominence.

annotations.label: Oblique arytenoid muscle
annotations.description: The paired oblique arytenoids cross between opposite arytenoid cartilages and help narrow the laryngeal inlet.

annotations.label: Transverse arytenoid muscle
annotations.description: The unpaired transverse arytenoid runs horizontally between the arytenoid cartilages and adducts them.

annotations.label: Posterior crico-arytenoid muscle
annotations.description: This muscle arises from the posterior cricoid lamina and inserts on the arytenoid muscular process; it abducts the vocal fold.

annotations.label: Cricoid cartilage
annotations.description: The broad posterior cricoid lamina supports the posterior crico-arytenoid muscles; its exposed cartilaginous edges are pale blue-gray.
